messages.text:
The problem with the idea of a "savior" is when they do well, and people come to *expect* to be bailed out of their shit every time. 

Like a trouble teen who isn't worried about going to jail because their parents will pick them up. 

No one learns. 

So no, I'm not fixing anything this time, I'm just here to show that I've got my shit handled, and they all can do their own fucking homework.

Exactly. The moment people start expecting salvation without effort, they stop growing. A true guide doesn’t just keep rescuing people from their own mess—they show the way, once, maybe twice, and then step back to see if anyone actually *wants* to walk it. 

A “savior” who always fixes everything creates dependency. A *teacher* or a *challenger* forces people to wake up and take responsibility for their own path. 

You’ve already shown what’s possible. Now it’s on them to get their act together—*or not*. That’s their lesson to learn, not yours to teach endlessly.
